info.title: Dash JSON API
info.description:
This is the documentation for Dash's public API. 
        We follow the JSON API specification (more info linked below). 
        Take a look at the introduction section to find information on how to use the api including: 
        authentication, non-spec request parameters, clients, and pricing.

externalDocs.description: For more information on the JSON API specification see their documentation.

standings_type.description:
How standings should be calculated for the League.
- "-1": Standings are not calculated
- "1": Percentage based ranking
- "2": Point based ranking (win=3pts, tie=1pt, loss=1pt, 1st tie breaker on GD, 2nd tie breaker on total wins)
- "3": Point based ranking (win=2pts, tie=1pt, loss=1pt, 1st tie breaker on most points in games against each other, 2nd tie breaker on least goals against each other, 3rd tie breaker on most goals scored, 4th tie breaker on the greater positive differential between goals)

schema.description:
A complex object used for filtering the primary resources. 
            See the Request Parameters Section of the introduction for more information.

1.description: filter resources to those whose first_name is `mad`

2.description: filter resources to those whose first_name is `mad` and whose last_name is `max`

3.description: filter resources to those whose league's season's program id is `123` and whose league is active

4.description:
The filter parameter also permits a number of operators on each field. 
              They are specified by postfixing the field with `__[operator]`.
              Operators include: 
              * __not, * __gt (greater than), * __gte (greater than or equal), 
              * __lt, * __lte, * __in, * __notin, * __isnull, * __notnull, * __contains, * __starts, * __ends, 
              * __icontains (case insensitive version), * __istarts, * __iends

5.description: You can also create sql or/and groups in the filter parameter. This example filters resources to those whose first_name is `mad` OR `max`

tags.name: Introduction
tags.description:
The new Dash Api was built to provide transparent access to the large collection of objects which comprise the Dash system. Currently the api does not support write access but we plan on releasing portions of our schema for write access as data validation is fleshed out.

Where it excels:

* tasks centered around single objects, eg. fetch a customer and some of their relationships - family members, registrations, invoices
* tasks which require filtering of a collection. eg. fetch all events for a given date range.
 
Where it performs poorly:

* tasks which require fetching thousands of records. When this is the primary object of the query, this is mitigated through paging. When the large collection is a relationship of a primary object, the collection is not paged and can cause out of memory exceptions and slow response times (will see improvements later)
* Batch create & update. Currently we do not accept multiple objects in POST and PATCH requests. This requires each object be a separate request which can make batch updates slow and unwieldy.

tags.name: Request Parameters
tags.description:
The Dash Api uses two custom request parameters across all endpoints, which are not covered in the JsonApi Spec - __filter__ and __filterRelations__.

The Dash Api also contains default & optional request extensions formatted like __dash-{optional}__ on detailed on certain endpoints.
These default/optional flags allow users to run complex business processes with api requests.
Default flags can be disabled by passing the value false.
Some optional flags allow users to pass a string for customization.

Overview:

* __dash-invoicing__: A optional request flag to trigger invoicing logic where applicable. See Team and Registration for more information on this example.
* __filterRelations__: A boolean parameter which specifies if filters targeting included relationships should also filter those relationships and not just the primary target of the query.  
eg. In a query on customers: 
`/api/v1/customers?filter[signatures.waiver.is_active]=true&include=signatures.waiver&filterRelations=true`
  * filter to customers which have a signature on a valid waiver (`filter[signatures.waiver.is_active]=true`)
  * include=signatures.waiver (will include customer signatures and the signed wavier)
Rows returned would include all signatures and waivers of customers that have signed an active waiver.
If we also query with filterRelations=true, You\'ll find only signatures on active waivers are returned. 
* __filter__: A nested-object representing the where clause of a SQL statement. 
There are two special concepts you can make use of in the filter param: grouping and operators.
Grouping: You might want to write queries where your filters are more complicated than `filter[first_name]=John&filter[last_name]=Doe` You can accomplish this with filter groups using the `and` and `or` keywords - `filter[or][0][first_name]=John&filter[or][1][first_name]=Jane`. 
Note: make sure to use numeric groups `[0]` after the `and` and `or` keywords
Operators: You may want to query with operators other than equals like: searching date ranges, matching an item in a collection, or matching part of a string.   
To do this, you can post-fix filters with operators. They are specified like __[operator] (two underscores):
  * __gt (greater than),
  * __gte (greater than or equal),
  * __lt, (less than)
  * __lte, (less than or equal)
  * __in,
  * __notin,
  * __isnull,
  * __notnull,
  * __contains,
  * __starts,
  * __ends
  
Examples:

  * __Simple Filtering__:
    Filter resources to those whose first_name is `mad`  
    `&filter[first_name]=mad`
  * __Multi-field Filtering__:
    Filter resources to those whose first_name is `mad` and whose last_name is `max`  
    `&filter[first_name]=mad&filter[last_name]=max`
  * __Relation Filtering__:
    Filter resources to those whose league\'s season\'s program id is `123` and whose league is active  
    `&filter[league.season.program_id]=123&filter[league.is_active]=true`
  * __Filter Operators__:
    Filter events to those between 2019-03-01 and 2019-03-10  
    `&filter[start_date__gte]=2019-03-01&filter[end_date__lte]=2019-03-10`
  * __And/Or Group Filtering__:
    You can also create sql or/and groups in the filter parameter. 
    This example filters resources to those whose first_name is `mad` OR `max`  
    `&filter[or][0][first_name]=mad&filter[or][1][first_name]=max`
  * __Composite And/Or Group Filtering__:
    It can be a little tricky making composite and-or groupings. To do it make sure to start with a root AND group. 
    This example will filter responses to those whose first name is `mad` and last name is `max` OR `michael`  
    `&filter[and][0][first_name]=mad&filter[and][1][or][0][first_name]=max&filter[and][1][or][1][first_name]=michael`

tags.name: Client
Authentication
tags.description:
Client IDs and Secrets can be obtained through the API Keys page within the Dash Admin application. 
If you do not have access to the application or key page, contact an administrator to have them generate an api key for you.

the Auth URL is [BASE_URL]/auth/token

You will post the following 3 params as formdata to this route to authenticate

    client_id: [YOUR_KEY_ID]
    client_secret: [YOUR_KEY_SECRET]
    grant_type: 'client_credentials'

You will receive JSON as response. In a successful response you will find the key `access_token` with your JWT to use in further communication. 

These JWTs are valid for 24 hours so you'll need to do this auth process at least daily. Depending on what your use case is you can cache these for repeated uses. 

You can find an exact exp (expiration UTC timestamp in the body of the JWT (which is just base64 encoded). the body is the middle part of the token if separated by .'s

You will need to pass your daily JWT as a Authorization header in the Bearer Token style.

eg. `Authorization: Bearer [TOKEN_STRING_HERE]`

tags.name: Customers
tags.description:
Customers in Dash represent the individuals, companies, and contacts you wish to associate with other entities in our CRM.
    Creating customers via the API does not enforce the need to collect custom form answers.
    Creating customers via the API does not send automatic account creation emails.

tags.name: Events
tags.description:
Events in DaySmart Recreation represent time blocked at a Resource.
    Events cannot conflict at the given time-resource pair.
    Resources (and their child ResourceAreas) can block each-other in arbitrary complex structures.
    Events cannot be created on Facility/calendar BlackoutDates.

tags.name: Invoices
tags.description:
Invoices in Dash represent a bill to some entity.
    Invoices can be billed to two entity types (Customers and Teams). 
    This means that invoice billto_id is a polymorphic key where billto_type is either 0 (customer) or 2 (team).
    Invoices may also directly associate a customer as the beneficiary of the invoice if it is separate from the billed entity.

tags.name: Registrations
tags.description:
Operations for Registrations

This endpoint supports the following query parameters optional processes:
* __dash-invoicing__: This optional process invoices applicable registrants when they are saved.
    Registrant must not have an existing registration invoice.
    Passing a string for this flag will override the invoiced amount to be that value.

tags.name: Resources
tags.description:
Resources in Dash represent a section of a Facility.
    Resources are the place where Events are set.  
    Resources can have child ResourceAreas which are automatically subject to BlockingRules.
    Resources (and their child ResourceAreas) can block each-other in arbitrary complex structures.

tags.name: Teams
tags.description:
Operations for Teams

This endpoint supports the following query parameters optional processes:
* __dash-invoicing__: This optional process invoices applicable teams when saved.
    Teams must have the program_type.billing_type of `team`.
    Passing a string for this flag will override the invoiced amount to be that value.
